target.title: fix(ui): turn large pasted text into compact composer attachments
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users pasting large plain-text blocks into the Control UI chat composer would dump the entire block into the textarea, making the composer hard to scan and easy to send accidentally.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change treats plain-text paste payloads over 2000 characters as existing composer attachments with `text/plain` file payloads instead of introducing a separate composer-only state model. That keeps send, queue, retry, payload snapshotting, removal, and cleanup on the existing attachment path; the compact preview adds a “show in composer” action for users who want to edit the pasted text inline.

Normal short text paste behavior is unchanged, and the existing data-URL/image paste path is checked before large text handling so image paste behavior continues to use the current attachment flow.

## User Impact

Users can paste large text into chat without the textarea becoming unwieldy. The pasted text appears as a compact block, can be removed, can be expanded back into the composer, and is still included in the submitted chat payload when left as a block.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.test.ts` (`203` tests passed)
- Browser smoke on `pnpm dev:ui:mock -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5199`:
  - pasted >2000 characters and verified a compact pasted-text block appeared while the textarea stayed empty
  - removed the pasted-text block
  - pasted again and used “show in composer”; verified the full text returned to the textarea and the block was removed
- Send payload preservation is covered by the focused `handleSendChat` regression test for `text/plain` pasted-text attachments.
